source: E. M. Standish, Keplerian Elements for Approximate Positions of the Major Planets, JPL Solar System Dynamics, Table 1 (valid 1800-2050): https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/planets/approx_pos.html
radii_source: Mean radii from NASA's planetary fact sheets: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/
note: Elements at J2000 (JD 2451545.0) with their rates per Julian century; angles in degrees, a in AU. omega_bar is the longitude of perihelion, so the argument of perihelion is omega_bar - Omega. Earth's row is the Earth-Moon barycentre.

bodies.name: Sun
bodies.texture: NASA's Sun model (Eyes on the Solar System)

regions.name: Main asteroid belt
regions.why: Between Mars and Jupiter: bodies that never formed a planet, held between the 4:1 and 2:1 resonances with Jupiter.

regions.name: Kirkwood gap 3:1
regions.why: An asteroid here would orbit three times for each of Jupiter's one; the repeated pull clears it.

regions.name: Kirkwood gap 2:1
regions.why: Two orbits for Jupiter's one: the belt's outer edge.

regions.name: Hilda group 3:2
regions.why: Locked in the 3:2 resonance, so they gather in a triangle with Jupiter at one corner.

regions.name: Jupiter trojans
regions.why: Sharing Jupiter's orbit, 60° ahead (L4) and behind (L5).
